newsitem.title: GERMANY: German metal employers/unions to meet again Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: German metal employers/unions to meet again Oct 10.

text.p: Employers and unions meeting to discuss the issue of sick-pay cuts issued a joint statement on Monday evening to say they would meet again on October 10.
The metal and electronics industry union Gesamtmetall said it was recommending that its members not cut sick pay to employees for the time being.
For its side, the metal and electronics trade union IG Metall urged its members not to stage protests at companies unless sick pay is cut.
IG Metall chairman Klaus Zwickel said "We are just as interested as Gesamtmetall in achieving as rapid a clarification of the situation as possible."
Gesamtmetall president Werner Stumpfe said after the reading of the joint statement that Monday's agreement was "neutral for both sides".
Zwickel said the aim of the talks was to ensure that "a very highly-explosive situation did not escalate."

German unions have been angered by a new law reducing sick pay to 80 percent from 100 percent, aimed at cutting labour costs. The unions say such benefits have been hard won in negotiation and cannot be simply abolished overnight.
